listenings.text: Right, sit down. Three things. Your first wave was a mistake and you know it was, because you told me before the heat that you were going to wait for the sets. You did not wait. Second, your take-off is too slow, and it has been too slow all season, so that is what we work on from Monday. Third, and I am only saying this once: the conditions were difficult for everybody out there and you were the only one who read the tide correctly. Do not tell anybody I said that.

So what did he say? Tell me everything. Right, so he said your first wave was a mistake, which honestly everybody could see. And he told you that your take-off has been too slow all season, which is fair. But then he said you were the only one who read the tide correctly, and he asked you not to repeat it? That is the biggest compliment that man has given anybody this year. My brother trained with him for three seasons and he told me he never once said anything nice. Not once.

reading.rtitle: Three people, one heat, three versions
paras: After the semifinal, three different people said something about the same twenty minutes of surfing, and none of the three said the same thing.

The coach was direct, as always. He said that the first wave had been a mistake and that I had been too slow on the take-off. Then he admitted that the conditions had been difficult for everybody, which for him counts as praise.

The judge was kinder. She told me that my second wave had been the best one of the heat and that the score had been close. She also mentioned that the tide had been dropping fast, and that most of the field had not noticed it.

My host mum did not talk about surfing at all. She said that I looked tired, that I had not eaten since breakfast, and that we were going home. Then she made a promise: next time she would bring sandwiches.
Three versions of the same heat. The coach gave me feedback, the judge gave me information, and my host mum gave me a warning about lunch. All three were right.
